Apple Pay is a must-have feature for iPhone users when shopping at physical stores, online stores, and apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even more useful. Here is how these features work, as well as a major expansion that has already begun rolling out.

iOS 27 new design

One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it easier to switch between different credit cards when checking out on websites and apps.

With the new design, you can easily swipe between different credit cards on the main Apple Pay checkout screen. You can also tap on a card to see a grid view of all your available Apple Pay credit cards.

The new design also makes it easier to view details of individual credit cards, including rewards, balances, buy-now-pay-later options, and more.

iOS 27 was officially released to all users last week. You can update through the "Settings" app on your iPhone.

American Express Membership Rewards

Apple and American Express previously announced a new partnership that allows you to pay using American Express Membership Rewards points.

When you shop online or in apps using your American Express card, you will see a new "Use Rewards" option on the checkout screen, along with your available Membership Rewards points balance. You can use points to pay for all or part of your purchase directly within the Apple Pay checkout flow.

American Express points redeemed through Apple Pay are worth 0.7 US cents each. For example, 10,000 points can be converted into US$70, which will be deducted from your purchase amount.

Tap to Share

In iOS 27, Apple has added a new "Tap to Share" feature that integrates with Apple Pay on iPhone, applicable to in-store purchases.

This feature is an extension of "Tap to Pay on iPhone". Apple explains:

Customers only need a single tap to connect to a participating merchant's iPhone, for a more personalized and faster in-store shopping experience, and can securely share information such as email addresses, other contact details, shipping addresses, membership rewards information, and more. Customers can also view the items in their shopping basket in real time, making it easy to track purchased items and ensure all discounts and offers are applied correctly.

Once completed, customers can complete checkout with Apple Pay on their own iPhone.

Topping up debit cards

iPhone users at select banks can manage their debit card balances directly within the Apple Pay interface. According to Apple, you can top up supported debit cards directly with Apple Pay, either within Apple Wallet or at checkout.

Additional news: Apple Pay lands at Walmart

This isn't actually a new feature developed by Apple itself, but rather something that should have been implemented many years ago and has finally become a reality. Walmart has announced that it has finally begun rolling out support for Apple Pay. Apple Pay will also be rolled out at Sam's Club alongside this initiative.

Walmart has begun rolling out Apple Pay (as well as broader contactless payment support) in Arkansas this week. The retailer said it will be officially launched at all stores nationwide in the US by the end of this year.

Conclusion

As Apple Pay becomes more widespread and popular among retailers, it is pleasing to see Apple continuing to improve the user experience. For me personally, whether shopping online or in physical stores, Apple Pay is my preferred checkout payment method.

How often do you use Apple Pay? What are your favorite Apple Pay features? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
